mainTopic: The punishments of the מוציא שם רע: their sources, conditions, and the dispute over whether relations are required
overview: This amud deals with the מוציא שם רע, a husband who falsely claims his new wife was unfaithful. רב פפא shows that the word לוקה can mean paying money, and proves it from a vow of 'half my ערך.' A ברייתא then teaches that וענשו means the money fine and ויסרו means מלקות; רבי אבהו proves the lashes through a chain of word-links. רבי אלעזר and רבי נתן disagree about which פסוק is the warning against slander. The husband is punished only if he asked the witnesses to testify, while רבי יהודה requires that he hired them, learned through a גזירה שוה from the laws of interest. רבי ירמיה and רב אשי ask about the limits of these rules; one question is solved: accusing her about her marriage to his brother does not count. Next comes the dispute between the רבנן and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב on whether the husband must have had relations with her, and how each side reads the פסוקים. Finally, רבי יוחנן rules that the husband is liable only if he was with her, and the גמרא begins asking whose view this follows; the discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: רב פפא: 'He is flogged' means he pays money
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that 'לוקה' in the earlier ברייתא refers to paying the money fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: What does it mean when it was taught there, 'if he had relations, he is flogged'? It means money.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains a word in a ברייתא quoted earlier: when it says the husband is 'לוקה,' it really means he pays the money fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally לוקה means getting lashes (מלקות). רב פפא says that in this ברייתא it points to the 100-silver fine of the מוציא שם רע. So the condition 'only if he had relations' applies to the money payment.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
What is the 'if he had relations, he is flogged' that is taught there?
It means money.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אָמַר: מַאי ״בָּעַל לוֹקֶה״ דְּקָתָנֵי הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a new reading of a ברייתא discussed before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In that ברייתא, לוקה refers to the monetary fine, not lashes.

steps.title: Can money be called flogging?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether a money payment can be called מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And do we call money 'flogging'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב פפא: the word for flogging does not seem to fit a money payment.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge targets the wording. If a source says 'flogged,' the plain meaning is lashes, so calling a fine 'flogging' seems forced.

phrases.english: And does one call money 'flogging'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רב פפא's reading in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's claim that לוקה means paying money
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word for lashes should not be used to describe a payment of money.

steps.title: Proof from the vow of 'half my ערך'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers yes and quotes רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, who says one who vows half his ערך is 'לוקה' and pays the full ערך.
steps.simpleTranslation: Yes, and we learned: One who says 'Half my ערך is upon me' gives half his ערך. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says: He is flogged and gives a full ערך.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says yes, money can be called flogging, and brings a source where the word לוקה appears in a case about money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא says he pays exactly half his ערך. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says 'לוקה' and pays the full ערך. Nothing here seems to deserve lashes, which sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: a fixed valuation set by the Torah by age and gender, given to the מקדש
'half my valuation is upon me,' a vow

phrases.english: Yes, and we learned:
'One who says: Half my valuation is upon me'
gives half his valuation.
Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, says:
He is flogged and gives a full valuation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by bringing a source.
steps.raayaObject: That the word לוקה can describe a money payment
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ruling of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה on one who vows half his ערך

steps.title: Why would he be flogged?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what sin the person committed that would deserve lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why is he flogged?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says he is flogged. This sets up רב פפא's answer, which completes the proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Making a vow of half his ערך is not a sin. So real lashes make no sense here, which pushes us to read לוקה differently.

phrases.english: Why is he flogged?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the wording of the source quoted in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does לוקה mean in רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה's ruling?

steps.title: He is 'flogged' by paying the full ערך
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that לוקה there means he is hit with paying the full ערך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: He is 'flogged' with a full valuation.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא answers that the 'flogging' is the extra money: he has to pay the full ערך instead of half.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This completes the proof from step 3. A money penalty can be called לוקה, so רב פפא's reading in step 1 is not forced.

keyTerms.meaning: is 'struck' with paying a full valuation

steps.whatToRemember: The word לוקה can sometimes mean being hit with a money penalty, not only lashes.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
He is flogged with a full valuation.
phrases.notes: He means the 'lashes' are the extra payment he has to make.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: לוֹקֶה בְּעֵרֶךְ שָׁלֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 and closes the proof for step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: לוקה there means paying the full ערך, so money can be called flogging.

steps.title: Reason for paying the full ערך: a rabbinic decree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the full ערך is a decree, so people will not confuse 'half my ערך' with 'the ערך of half of me.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? It is a decree about 'half his ערך' because of 'the ערך of half of him.' And 'the ערך of half of him' counts as a body part that life depends on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks and answers why רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה makes him pay a full ערך. It is a גזירה, a protective rabbinic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If someone vows 'the ערך of half of me,' that half includes vital organs like the heart, so it counts as a vow of his whole ערך. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה holds that a rabbinic decree makes even 'half my ערך' cost a full ערך, so people won't mix up the two phrases. The תנא קמא makes no such decree, so in his view he pays only half.

keyTerms.meaning: a protective decree of the רבנן
because of, out of concern for
the valuation of half of himself
a body part that life depends on

steps.confusionAlert: 'חצי ערכו' (half of his valuation) and 'ערך חציו' (the valuation of half of his body) sound almost the same but are different vows. The first is half the money. The second, by Torah law, is the full amount.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
It is a decree on 'half his valuation'
because of 'the valuation of half of him.'
And 'the valuation of half of him' counts as
a body part on which life depends.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא — גְּזֵירָה ״חֲצִי עֶרְכּוֹ״ אַטּוּ ״עֵרֶךְ חֶצְיוֹ״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the ruling used as proof in steps 3–5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A rabbinic decree, so 'half my ערך' is not confused with 'the ערך of half of me,' which by law requires the full ערך.

steps.title: ברייתא: וענשו means money, ויסרו means lashes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads the פסוקים of מוציא שם רע: 'וענשו אותו' refers to the money fine, and 'ויסרו' refers to מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'And they shall fine him' means money; 'and they shall chastise' means flogging.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that gives a source in the פסוקים for each punishment of the מוציא שם רע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוקים use two words, ויסרו and וענשו. The ברייתא links each word to a different punishment: one to money and one to lashes.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the Torah basis for the two punishments of the מוציא שם רע: the 100-silver fine and מלקות.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
'And they shall fine him': this is money,
phrases.notes: דברים 22:19

phrases.english: 'and they shall chastise': this is flogging.
phrases.notes: דברים 22:18

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the sources for the punishments of the מוציא שם רע.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: וענשו refers to the money fine; ויסרו refers to מלקות.

steps.title: Money is clear, but where do we learn ויסרו means lashes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא agrees that וענשו clearly means money, since the פסוק mentions 100 silver, but asks how we know ויסרו means מלקות.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense that 'וענשו' means money, since it is written: 'And they shall fine him a hundred silver and give it to the girl's father.' But 'ויסרו' means flogging: from where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the first half of the ברייתא and asks for a source for the second half. This sets up the next step, which will give the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With וענשו, the פסוק itself names a sum of money, so the meaning is clear. ויסרו just means 'chastise' and could mean many things. So the גמרא asks how we know it means lashes.

phrases.english: Granted, 'and they shall fine' is money,
as it is written: 'And they shall fine him a hundred silver'
'and give it to the father of the girl.'
phrases.notes: דברים 22:19

phrases.english: But 'and they shall chastise' is flogging:
from where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the second half of the ברייתא in step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that ויסרו refers to מלקות.

steps.title: רבי אבהו links ויסרו to lashes through a chain of words
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו proves that ויסרו means מלקות by linking it to the same word in the בן סורר ומורה פסוק, then to the word בן there, and then to the similar word בִּן in the פסוק about lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: We learn 'they shall chastise' here from 'they shall chastise' by the rebellious son. That 'chastise' we explain from the word 'son' in the same פסוק. And 'son' (בן) we explain from 'deserves' (בִּן) in the פסוק: 'And it shall be, if the wicked man deserves to be flogged.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question from step 8: how do we know ויסרו means מלקות? He gives a chain of three word-links that ends at a פסוק that clearly talks about lashes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Link 1: ויסרו by מוציא שם רע matches ויסרו by בן סורר ומורה. Link 2: in that פסוק, ויסרו sits next to the word בן. Link 3: בן looks like בִּן in 'בִּן הכות הרשע', which openly talks about flogging, so ויסרו means lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: son, from the פסוק of the rebellious son
deserves, in the פסוק about lashes

steps.confusionAlert: Don't look for a single direct proof. Each link only connects two matching words, and only the last link reaches a פסוק that openly mentions flogging.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
We learned 'they shall chastise' from 'they shall chastise,'
phrases.notes: The second יסרו is in the פסוק about the rebellious son, דברים 21:18.

phrases.english: and 'chastise' from 'son,'
and 'son' from 'deserves' —
phrases.notes: The two words are spelled the same, בן, so one is learned from the other.

phrases.english: 'And it shall be, if the wicked man deserves to be flogged.'
phrases.notes: דברים 25:2

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 8 about the source that ויסרו means מלקות.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A chain of word-links (יסרו–יסרו, יסרו–בן, בן–בִּן) connects ויסרו to the פסוק of flogging.
steps.whatToRemember: ויסרו in the פרשה of מוציא שם רע means מלקות, learned through רבי אבהו's chain of three word-links.

steps.title: Where is the warning against slandering?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the Torah's warning (אזהרה) that the מוציא שם רע breaks.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know the warning against a person who spreads a bad name?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know the slanderer gets lashes, the גמרא asks which Torah prohibition he broke. This sets up the two answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lashes are normally given only for breaking a לאו, a Torah warning. So the punishment we just found needs a matching prohibition, and the גמרא looks for it.

keyTerms.meaning: a warning; the Torah prohibition behind a punishment
one who spreads a false bad name about his wife

phrases.english: The warning for one who spreads a bad name, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the punishment (מלקות) to the prohibition that punishment requires.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which פסוק is the אזהרה for מוציא שם רע.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: from 'Do not go as a talebearer'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says the warning is 'לא תלך רכיל'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: from 'You shall not go about as a talebearer.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives his source for the warning: the general prohibition against going around telling tales.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spreading a false bad name is a kind of harmful talk about someone. So רבי אלעזר places it under the לאו of רכילות.

keyTerms.meaning: a talebearer, someone who goes around spreading talk

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
From 'You shall not go about as a talebearer.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:16

steps.relationToPreviousStep: First answer to the question of step 10.

steps.title: רבי נתן: from 'Guard yourself from every evil thing'
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן says the warning is 'ונשמרת מכל דבר רע'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי נתן says: from 'And you shall guard yourself from every evil thing.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי נתן gives a different פסוק as the source for the warning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads 'דבר רע', an evil thing, as also meaning evil speech, since דבר can mean a word. So slander falls under this warning.

keyTerms.meaning: an evil thing, read here as evil speech

phrases.english: Rabbi Natan says:
From 'And you shall guard yourself from every evil thing.'
phrases.notes: דברים 23:10. דבר can also mean 'word', so he reads it as evil speech.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, competing answer to the same question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The warning is 'ונשמרת מכל דבר רע'.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי אלעזר use רבי נתן's פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי אלעזר did not learn the warning from 'ונשמרת מכל דבר רע'.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר, what is the reason he did not say it from this פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts checking the disagreement by asking why רבי אלעזר passes over רבי נתן's פסוק. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'דבר רע' can mean evil speech, it looks like a good source. So the גמרא expects רבי אלעזר to need that פסוק for something else.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar, what is the reason
that he did not say it from this one?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר מֵהַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Examines רבי אלעזר's side of the disagreement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי אלעזר does with the פסוק 'ונשמרת מכל דבר רע'.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר uses that פסוק for רבי פנחס בן יאיר's teaching
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר needs 'ונשמרת מכל דבר רע' for רבי פנחס בן יאיר, who learns from it that a person should not have impure thoughts by day and come to טומאה at night.
steps.simpleTranslation: He needs that פסוק for the teaching of רבי פנחס בן יאיר. 'And you shall guard yourself from every evil thing': from here רבי פנחס בן יאיר said, a person should not have impure thoughts by day and come to impurity at night.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר uses this פסוק for a different lesson, so it is not free to teach the warning against slander.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק sits in the section about a man who becomes טמא at night in the army camp. רבי פנחס בן יאיר reads 'guard yourself from every evil thing' as guarding your thoughts by day so you don't come to that טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: the תנא whose teaching is quoted

phrases.english: He needs that one
for the teaching of Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair.
'And you shall guard yourself from every evil thing,'

phrases.aramaic: מִכָּאן אָמַר רַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר:
phrases.english: from here Rabbi Pinchas ben Yair said:
A person should not have improper thoughts by day
and come to impurity at night.
phrases.notes: He means the impurity of an emission at night.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא מִיבְּעֵי לֵיהּ לְכִדְרַבִּי פִּנְחָס בֶּן יָאִיר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר uses that פסוק for רבי פנחס בן יאיר's warning about thoughts that lead to טומאה at night.

steps.title: Why doesn't רבי נתן use רבי אלעזר's פסוק?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the reverse question: why didn't רבי נתן learn the warning from 'לא תלך רכיל'?
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי נתן, what is the reason he did not say it from that פסוק?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא checks the other side and asks why רבי נתן passes over 'לא תלך רכיל'. This sets up the final answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Do not be a talebearer' looks like the most obvious source for a ban on harmful talk. So the גמרא expects רבי נתן to read it differently.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Natan, what is the reason
that he did not say it from this one?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי נָתָן מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר מֵהַאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The mirror question of step 13, now about רבי נתן.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי נתן does with the פסוק 'לא תלך רכיל'.

steps.title: רבי נתן reads רכיל as a warning to judges
steps.stepSummary: רבי נתן reads 'לא תלך רכיל' as a warning to בית דין not to be soft to one side and harsh to the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: That פסוק is a warning to the court that it should not be soft to this one and harsh to that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי נתן uses 'רכיל' for a different lesson about judges treating both sides equally, so it is not his source for slander.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He splits רכיל into 'רך ל-', soft to someone. So the פסוק tells judges not to be gentle with one side and tough with the other, and he needs his own פסוק for the slander warning.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree a מוציא שם רע breaks a Torah warning. They only disagree which פסוק is the source, because each one reads the other's פסוק as teaching a different lesson.

phrases.english: That one is a warning to the court
that it should not be soft to this one
phrases.notes: He is reading רכיל as 'רך ל-', soft toward someone.

phrases.english: and harsh to that one.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָהוּא: אַזְהָרָה לְבֵית דִּין שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא רַךְ לָזֶה וְקָשֶׁה לָזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 15 and completes the explanation of both opinions.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי נתן uses 'לא תלך רכיל' as a warning that judges must treat both sides equally.

steps.title: Witnesses who testified on their own: the husband is not punished
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if the husband did not ask the witnesses to testify, he is not flogged and does not pay the hundred סלעים, even if they turn out to be עדים זוממין.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the husband did not tell witnesses 'Come and testify for me,' but they testified for him on their own, he is not flogged and does not pay a hundred סלעים. She and her plotting witnesses are rushed to the stoning place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא about a מוציא שם רע. The witnesses came forward on their own, so the husband does not get the punishments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The punishments of a מוציא שם רע (מלקות and a hundred סלעים) depend on the husband being the one behind the testimony. Here he did not bring the witnesses, so even if they are proven liars, he is not to blame. The last line about stoning sounds strange, and the גמרא will fix it in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: on their own, without being asked
the 100-סלע fine a מוציא שם רע pays

phrases.english: If he did not say to witnesses
"Come and testify for me,"
but they testify for him on their own —
he is not flogged,
and does not give a hundred סלעים.
She and her plotting witnesses
are brought early to the stoning place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא about the מוציא שם רע, after the discussion of the לאו ended in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: If the husband did not bring the witnesses, he gets no מלקות and pays no hundred סלעים.

steps.title: Can both the wife and her witnesses be stoned?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the wording 'she and her plotting witnesses': both cannot be stoned.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'She and her plotting witnesses'? Could you really think that?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the words of the ברייתא. It makes no sense that both she and her witnesses get stoned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the witnesses told the truth, she is stoned and they are not liars. If they are proven עדים זוממין, they are stoned and she goes free. So 'she and her witnesses' together cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: could it enter your mind? (meaning: that can't be)

phrases.english: She and her plotting witnesses
could that enter your mind?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the last line of the ברייתא in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'היא וזוממיה מקדימין לבית הסקילה'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Only one side can be guilty: if she is guilty the witnesses are truthful; if the witnesses are liars, she is innocent.

steps.title: It means either she or her witnesses
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא: either the wife or her lying witnesses will be stoned.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather: either she or her plotting witnesses are brought early to the stoning place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the reading. One of them will be stoned, depending on who is telling the truth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the testimony is true, she is stoned as a נערה המאורסה who sinned. If the witnesses are proven זוממין, they get the punishment they tried to bring on her, which is סקילה. The point is that the husband stays out of it either way.

phrases.english: Rather: either she or her plotting witnesses
are brought early to the stoning place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18 by rereading the phrase.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say both she and the witnesses are stoned.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means one or the other: she if they told the truth, they if they lied.

steps.title: Asking witnesses is enough, unlike רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא learns from the ברייתא that if the husband asked the witnesses, he is punished even without paying them. This disagrees with רבי יהודה, who requires hiring.
steps.simpleTranslation: The reason is that he did not tell them. But if he told them, even though he did not hire them, he is punished. This rules out רבי יהודה, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says he is not liable unless he hires witnesses.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads a hidden lesson out of the ברייתא: just asking the witnesses is enough to make the husband liable. It then names who disagrees: רבי יהודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא exempts the husband only because he said nothing to the witnesses. That suggests that if he did ask them, he is punished, even with no payment. רבי יהודה disagrees and says he is punished only if he paid them.

keyTerms.meaning: the reason is (used to draw an inference)

phrases.english: The reason is that he did not tell them,
but if he told them,
even though he did not hire them, he is liable.
This rules out רבי יהודה's view.
As a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says:
He is not liable unless he hires witnesses.

steps.triggerLanguage: טַעְמָא דְּלָא אֲמַר לְהוּ הָא אֲמַר לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the main ruling of step 17 and draws an inference from it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By the ברייתא, a husband who asks witnesses to testify falsely is liable even without paying them, against רבי יהודה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets up the question of where רבי יהודה gets his need for hiring, which the next steps answer.

steps.title: What is רבי יהודה's source?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יהודה requires that the husband hire the witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of רבי יהודה?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks where רבי יהודה learns that the husband must have paid the witnesses. It is setting up רבי אבהו's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק never says the husband hired anyone. So the גמרא wants to know what source makes רבי יהודה add this condition.

phrases.english: What is the reason of רבי יהודה?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבי יהודה's view cited in step 20.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source for requiring that the husband hire the witnesses.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: a גזירה שוה on the word 'placing'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that רבי יהודה learns a גזירה שוה from the word 'שימה', which links our פסוק to the פסוק about interest. Just as that one is about money, so is ours.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: It is learned from 'placing' and 'placing.' Here it says: 'And he places wanton charges against her,' and there it says: 'Do not place interest upon him.' Just as there it is about money, so too here it is about money.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו gives רבי יהודה's source. The same word 'placing' appears in two פסוקים, so one teaches about the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וְשָׂם' in the פרשה of מוציא שם רע matches 'תְשִׂימוּן' in the פסוק about נשך, interest. Since the interest פסוק is about money, the גזירה שוה teaches that our case also involves money. So the husband must have paid the witnesses.

keyTerms.meaning: 'placing', the shared word in both פסוקים
just as there... so too here (the form of a גזירה שוה)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא says asking the witnesses is enough to make the husband a מוציא שם רע. רבי יהודה says he must have hired them, and learns it from the word 'שימה', which links to the money of נשך.
steps.confusionAlert: The גזירה שוה does not say the husband pays interest. It only borrows the idea that this 'placing' involves money, meaning he paid the witnesses.

phrases.english: רבי אבהו said:
It is learned from "placing" and "placing."
It is written here:
"And he places wanton charges against her,"
phrases.notes: דברים 22:14

phrases.english: and it is written there:
"Do not place interest upon him,"
phrases.notes: שמות 22:24

phrases.english: just as there it is about money,
so too here it is about money.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אַתְיָא שִׂימָה שִׂימָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה from 'שימה' links מוציא שם רע to נשך: just as נשך involves money, so the husband must have spent money hiring the witnesses.

steps.title: Support for the שימה-שימה derivation
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק reports that רב יוסף צידוני taught the same גזירה שוה of שימה-שימה in the school of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: רב יוסף צידוני also taught this in the school of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: we learn it from the word 'placing' here and the word 'placing' there.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an older teaching that says the same thing רבי אבהו just said, to support it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 22, רבי אבהו explained that רבי יהודה learns from a גזירה שוה. Now we see that this same גזירה שוה was already taught in the school of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי. So רבי אבהו's explanation is not a new idea; it has an older source behind it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Placing' — the shared word that links the two פסוקים
Taught (a teaching from the time of the תנאים)
The study hall of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said:
And so Rav Yosef Tzidoni taught
in the school of Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai:
It is learned from 'placing' and 'placing.'
phrases.notes: One 'placing' is about the husband who 'places' false charges on her (דברים 22:14). The other is 'do not place interest on him' (שמות 22:24).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up רבי אבהו's explanation in Step 22 with an older teaching.
steps.raayaObject: רבי אבהו's claim that רבי יהודה learns from the גזירה שוה of שימה-שימה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A teaching of רב יוסף צידוני from the school of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי.

steps.title: What counts as hiring the witnesses?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ירמיה asks: if the husband hired the witnesses with land, with less than a פרוטה, or with one פרוטה for both of them, does he still count as having hired them?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה asked: If he hired them with land, what is the law? With less than a פרוטה's worth, what is the law? If he paid both of them one פרוטה together, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: Building on the link to the laws of interest, רבי ירמיה asks three questions about what kind of payment counts as 'hiring' the witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי יהודה learns 'hiring' from the laws of interest, maybe the same limits apply here. Interest is about money and needs at least a פרוטה, so maybe paying with land, or paying less than a פרוטה, does not count. If one פרוטה is split between two witnesses, each one gets less than a פרוטה, so that is also unclear. The גמרא leaves these questions open.

keyTerms.meaning: Asked (raised a question that needs solving)
The smallest coin that counts as money in halacha

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya asked:
If he hired them with land, what is the law?
With less than the value of a peruta, what is the law?
Both of them with one peruta, what is the law?
phrases.notes: One פרוטה split between two witnesses means each witness got less than a פרוטה.

steps.confusionAlert: These questions follow רבי יהודה's view only. According to the first opinion, the husband is punished even without paying, so these questions would not come up.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the interest link from Steps 22-23 to ask how far the comparison goes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether payment with land, with less than a פרוטה, or with one פרוטה for two witnesses counts as 'hiring' for רבי יהודה.

steps.title: Accusations about an earlier marriage or a brother's marriage
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks whether the laws of מוציא שם רע apply when the husband accuses his wife about their first marriage (before a divorce and remarriage), or about her marriage to his brother (in a case of יבום).
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי asked: If he gave her a bad name about the first marriage, what is the law? If he did so about his brother's marriage, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks two more questions, this time about which marriage the false accusation can be about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the husband claims his wife sinned during their own engagement. Here he either divorced and remarried her and accuses her about the first time, or he married her through יבום and accuses her about the time she was engaged to his brother. The question is whether such claims still count as מוציא שם רע.

keyTerms.meaning: Spread a bad name (falsely accused her of sinning)

phrases.english: Rav Ashi asked:
If he spread a bad name
about the first marriage, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He married her, divorced her, then remarried her, and now accuses her about the first time around.

phrases.english: About his brother's marriage, what is the law?
phrases.notes: He married her through יבום and claims she sinned back when she was engaged to his brother.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another set of open questions about the limits of מוציא שם רע.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether מוציא שם רע applies to accusations about a previous marriage to the same man or about her marriage to his brother.

steps.title: The brother's-marriage case is solved: not to the יבם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers one of רב אשי's questions from רבי יונה's teaching: the פסוק says 'to this man,' and not to the יבם. So accusing her about his brother's marriage is not מוציא שם רע.
steps.simpleTranslation: Solve at least one of them, since רבי יונה taught: 'I gave my daughter to this man' — to this one, and not to the יבם.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the second question of רב אשי (about the brother's marriage) using a teaching about the wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father says in court, 'I gave my daughter to this man.' רבי יונה reads 'this man' as limiting: it means the husband she was given to, not a יבם who married her later. So if a יבם accuses her about her time with his brother, the special laws of מוציא שם רע do not apply. The question about the first marriage stays unanswered.

keyTerms.meaning: The brother who marries his brother's widow (יבום)

phrases.english: Solve at least one of them.
As Rabbi Yona taught:
'I gave my daughter to this man.'
phrases.notes: דברים 22:16

phrases.english: To this one, and not to the yavam.

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה learns 'hiring' from interest (שימה-שימה). רבי ירמיה's questions and רב אשי's first-marriage question stay open. But accusing her about his brother's marriage is not מוציא שם רע, because the פסוק says 'to this man.'
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the second half of רב אשי's question from Step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: An accusation about her marriage to his brother does not count as מוציא שם רע, since the פסוק limits it to 'this man' and not the יבם.

steps.title: What is the dispute between the רבנן and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks to see the actual מחלוקת between the רבנן and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב that was mentioned earlier.
steps.simpleTranslation: What do the רבנן say, and what does רבי אליעזר בן יעקב say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks to see exactly where the רבנן and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב disagree. This sets up the ברייתא that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Their dispute was mentioned earlier but never spelled out. The גמרא now wants the source text so we know exactly what each side holds.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא who disagrees with the רבנן here

phrases.aramaic: מַאי רַבָּנַן וּמַאי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב?
phrases.english: What is the view of the Rabbis, and what is the view of Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי רַבָּנַן וּמַאי רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: it asks for the source of a dispute mentioned earlier.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The exact content of the מחלוקת between the רבנן and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

steps.title: The ברייתא begins: how a case of defamation happens
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא that describes the husband's claim in court and the case of witnesses.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: How does הוצאת שם רע work? The husband comes to בית דין and says to the father, 'So-and-so, I did not find signs of virginity in your daughter.' If there are witnesses that she sinned while she was his, she has a כתובה of a מנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins answering by quoting a ברייתא that describes the husband coming to court with his complaint. The last line of this part will be challenged in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא sets up the case: the husband tells the father in court that his daughter was not a בתולה. It then says that if there are witnesses she sinned 'under him', she gets a כתובה of a מנה. That ruling sounds strange, and the גמרא will deal with it next.

keyTerms.meaning: Defaming her: a husband falsely claiming his new wife was not a virgin
Literally 'under him', meaning while she was already his betrothed
One hundred דינרים, the basic כתובה of a non-virgin

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita: How does a case of defamation work?
He came to the court and said:
'So-and-so, I did not find signs of virginity in your daughter.'
If there are witnesses that she sinned while she was his,
she has a marriage contract of a maneh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts answering step 27 by quoting the ברייתא that holds the dispute.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ברייתא that contains the מחלוקת, beginning with how the case of הוצאת שם רע plays out.

steps.title: How can a woman who sinned while betrothed just get a smaller marriage contract?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא stops the quote: a woman who sinned while betrothed deserves סקילה, so how can she simply collect a מנה?
steps.simpleTranslation: If there are witnesses that she sinned while she was his, she has a כתובה of a מנה?! She deserves stoning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא interrupts the ברייתא to challenge its last line. A betrothed woman who sins with witnesses deserves the death penalty, so talking about her כתובה makes no sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נערה המאורסה who sins with witnesses gets סקילה. Saying she just loses part of her כתובה ignores the much bigger punishment, so the line seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone who deserves death by stoning

phrases.english: If there are witnesses that she sinned while she was his,
she has a marriage contract of a maneh?!
She deserves stoning!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the last line of the ברייתא quoted in step 28.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's line that a woman with witnesses that she sinned 'under him' has a כתובה of a מנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A betrothed woman who sins with witnesses is חייבת סקילה, so the ברייתא should not be talking about her כתובה.

steps.title: Reading the ברייתא as two separate cases
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא really means two cases: sinning while betrothed brings סקילה, and sinning before אירוסין leaves her a כתובה of a מנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: If there are witnesses that she sinned while she was his, she gets stoning. If she sinned from the start, before she was betrothed, she has a כתובה of a מנה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the ברייתא is really describing two different cases. The מנה ruling belongs to a woman who sinned before she was betrothed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sinning after אירוסין is a capital sin, so that woman gets סקילה. A woman who sinned before אירוסין committed no capital sin. She only misled her husband about being a בתולה, so she gets a non-virgin's כתובה of a מנה instead of two hundred.

keyTerms.meaning: 'This is what it means': a reading that fills in the text
From the start, here meaning before she was betrothed

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read the מנה ruling as being about the woman who sinned while betrothed. It belongs to a different case: a woman who sinned before אירוסין.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ עֵדִים שֶׁזִּינְּתָה תַּחְתָּיו — בִּסְקִילָה.
phrases.english: If there are witnesses that she sinned while she was his, she is stoned.
If she sinned from the start,
phrases.notes: He means before she was betrothed, when she was still single.

phrases.english: she has a marriage contract of a maneh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the text as two separate cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to give only a reduced כתובה to a woman who sinned while betrothed.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sinning while betrothed brings סקילה. The מנה ruling is for a woman who sinned before אירוסין.

steps.title: The dispute: is a false accuser punished even if he never had relations with her?
steps.stepSummary: If the claim turns out false, the husband gets מלקות and pays a hundred סלעים. The רבנן say this applies either way; רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says only if he had relations with her.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it turns out the bad name is not a true bad name, he gets lashes and pays a hundred סלעים, whether or not he had relations with her. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: these rules were said only when he had relations with her.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and finally shows the dispute that step 27 asked about. It is about whether the husband's punishment depends on his having had relations with her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the husband's claim is proven false, the punishment is מלקות and a fine of a hundred סלעים. The רבנן (the unnamed first opinion) say he is punished even if he never had relations with her. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב limits the punishment to a husband who did.

keyTerms.meaning: A fine of one hundred סלעים paid to her father

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן: a false accuser is punished whether or not he had relations with her. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: only if he did.

phrases.english: If it turns out that the bad name is not a bad name,
phrases.notes: The corrected wording leaves out the letter in round brackets and uses the one in square brackets instead. It just means his claim was false.

phrases.english: he is lashed and gives one hundred sela,
whether he had relations with her or did not.
Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא נֶאֶמְרוּ דְּבָרִים הַלָּלוּ אֶלָּא כְּשֶׁבָּעַל.
phrases.english: These things were said only when he had relations with her.

steps.triggerLanguage: נִמְצָא שֵׁם רַע שֶׁאֵינוֹ שֵׁם רַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks the ברייתא back up after the side discussion in steps 29-30 and finishes answering step 27.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן: punished whether or not he had relations with her. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: only if he had relations with her.

steps.title: How do the רבנן read the פסוקים that speak of relations?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוקים say 'and he came to her' and 'I came near to her'. That fits רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, but how do the רבנן explain them?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, since it is written 'and he came to her' and 'and I came near to her.' But for the רבנן, what do 'and he came to her' and 'and I came near to her' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the רבנן from the wording of the פסוקים. The words seem to describe relations, which supports רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both phrases sound like they describe the husband having relations with her. If the רבנן punish him even when he did not, those words seem to have no purpose in their view.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It makes sense for': it works for one side, before the question on the other

phrases.english: It makes sense according to Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov,
that is why it is written: 'and he came to her,' 'and I came near to her,'
phrases.notes: דברים 22:13 and 22:14.

phrases.english: but according to the Rabbis,
what is meant by 'and he came to her,' 'and I came near to her'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the רבנן's view from step 31 using the wording of the פסוקים.
steps.kashyaTarget: The רבנן's view that he is punished even if he never had relations with her.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוקים use words that mean relations, which suggests the law only applies when he had relations with her.

steps.title: For the רבנן, the פסוקים mean false charges and words
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן read 'and he came to her' as coming with false charges, and 'I came near to her' as coming near with words.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he came to her' means with false accusations. 'And I came near to her' means with words.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for the רבנן by reading both phrases as not being about relations at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן read 'coming to her' as the husband coming at her with made-up charges, and 'coming near' as approaching her with talk. Since the פסוקים no longer require relations, the רבנן can punish him either way.
steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן read 'came to her' and 'came near to her' as false accusations and words, so in their view relations are not needed for the punishment.

phrases.english: 'And he came to her': with false charges,
'and I came near to her': with words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 32 on behalf of the רבנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different reading of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words 'came to her' and 'came near to her' seemed to mean relations.
steps.terutzMaskana: For the רבנן, they mean false charges and words, so relations are not required.

steps.title: How do the רבנן explain 'I did not find tokens of virginity'?
steps.stepSummary: The phrase 'I did not find in your daughter tokens of virginity' fits רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. What does it mean for the רבנן?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, because the פסוק says 'I did not find in your daughter tokens of virginity.' But for the רבנן, what does 'I did not find in your daughter tokens of virginity' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second phrase from the same פסוק. It seems to show that the husband did have relations with her, which would support רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says the husband had relations with her and found no signs of virginity, so this phrase fits him perfectly. The רבנן say the claim can be made even without relations. If so, how could the husband say he 'did not find' anything?

keyTerms.meaning: Granted / it makes sense (for one opinion)
That is what is written (the פסוק fits)

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov,
this is what is written:
"I did not find in your daughter tokens of virginity."
phrases.notes: דברים 22:17

phrases.english: But according to the Rabbis,
what is "I did not find in your daughter tokens of virginity"?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the challenge pattern of Step 32 using a new phrase from the פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view of the רבנן that the claim applies even without relations
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Not finding' signs of virginity suggests the husband had relations and checked, which the רבנן do not require.

steps.title: 'I did not find fitness of virginity'
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן read the phrase as 'I did not find your daughter fit as a virgin,' meaning she was unfaithful.
steps.simpleTranslation: It means: I did not find your daughter to have kosher, fitting virginity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for the רבנן. The husband is not talking about a physical check. He means he found out she was not faithful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By adding the word כשרי ('fitness of'), the רבנן turn the phrase from a physical finding into a legal claim. The husband found, through witnesses, that she sinned while betrothed. So no relations are needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Fitness of virginity: being faithful and properly a בתולה

phrases.english: I did not find for your daughter the fitness of virginity.
phrases.notes: The רבנן slip in one word, כשרי ('fitness'), so the husband is talking about her faithfulness, not a physical sign.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 34.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Not finding virginity' means a physical discovery after relations.
steps.terutzMaskana: It means not finding her faithful and fit, which can be known without relations.

steps.title: How do the רבנן explain 'these are my daughter's tokens of virginity'?
steps.stepSummary: The father's reply, 'these are the tokens of my daughter's virginity,' fits רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. What does it mean for the רבנן?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, because the פסוק says 'And these are the tokens of my daughter's virginity.' But for the רבנן, what does 'And these are the tokens of my daughter's virginity' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the רבנן again, this time from the father's answer to the husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, the father shows physical proof that she was a virgin. If there were no relations, as the רבנן allow, what physical 'tokens' could the father show?

keyTerms.meaning: The tokens of my daughter's virginity

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov,
this is what is written: "And these are the tokens of my daughter's virginity."
But according to the Rabbis,
what is "And these are the tokens of my daughter's virginity"?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב, הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב ״וְאֵלֶּה בְּתוּלֵי בִתִּי״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same challenge pattern, now on the father's reply.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The father showing 'tokens' suggests a physical sign from relations, which the רבנן do not require.

steps.title: 'These are the proofs of my daughter's fitness'
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן read the father's words as 'these are the proofs that my daughter was fit as a virgin.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It means: And these are the proofs of the fitness of my daughter's virginity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for the רבנן using the same word, כשרי. The father brings proof, like his own witnesses, that his daughter was faithful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just like the husband's claim in Step 35, the father's answer is about her faithfulness, not a physical sign. So the father can respond with witnesses even if there were no relations.

phrases.english: And these are the fitness of my daughter's virginity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 36 the same way Step 35 answered Step 34.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The father shows physical tokens from relations.
steps.terutzMaskana: The father shows proof that she was faithful, such as witnesses.

steps.title: How do the רבנן explain 'they shall spread the garment'?
steps.stepSummary: 'They shall spread the garment' fits רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. What does it mean for the רבנן?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, because the פסוק says 'And they shall spread the garment.' But for the רבנן, what does 'And they shall spread the garment' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings its strongest challenge: the פסוק talks about spreading out an actual cloth.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, the parents spread out the sheet from the wedding night to show it is stained, proving she was a virgin. If there were no relations, as the רבנן allow, there is no sheet to spread. Adding a word like כשרי will not solve this one.

keyTerms.meaning: And they shall spread the garment

phrases.english: Granted, according to Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov,
this is what is written: "And they shall spread the garment."
But according to the Rabbis,
what is "And they shall spread the garment"?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב, הַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב: ״וּפָרְשׂוּ הַשִּׂמְלָה״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third challenge in the same pattern, on the phrase about the garment.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Spreading a real cloth assumes a wedding-night sheet, which exists only if they had relations.

steps.title: רבי אבהו: 'Spread out what he placed against her'
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו reads שמלה (garment) as ששם לה (what he placed against her): examine the husband's charges.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: 'Spread out' what he placed against her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers for the רבנן with a wordplay. 'Spread the garment' means look closely at the accusations the husband put against her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word השמלה sounds like ששם לה, 'that he placed on her.' So 'spreading' means opening up and checking the husband's charges and witnesses. No physical cloth is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: What he placed against her (his accusations)
The אמורא who gives the answer here

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
Spread out what he placed against her.
phrases.notes: Say הַשִּׂמְלָה and שֶׁשָּׂם לָהּ out loud: they sound alike. That is the wordplay.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: פָּרְשׂוּ מַה שֶּׁשָּׂם לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 38.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Garment' means a real sheet from the wedding night.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Garment' hints to the charges the husband placed on her, which the court examines.

steps.title: A ברייתא: both sides bring witnesses, made clear like a new garment
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא supports רבי אבהו: 'spread the garment' means witnesses come from both sides and the court makes the matter clear like a new garment.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'And they shall spread the garment' teaches that the witnesses of this side come, and the witnesses of that side come, and the court clears up the matter like a new garment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that reads the פסוק the same non-literal way as רבי אבהו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says 'garment' is a picture: the husband's witnesses and the father's witnesses both testify, and the court makes the truth as clear as a clean, new cloth. This shows the רבנן's reading is an established teaching, not just a forced answer.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: As it is taught:
"And they shall spread the garment,"
this teaches that the witnesses of this one come,
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the husband, and 'that one' in the next line is the father.

phrases.english: and the witnesses of that one,
and they clarify the matter
like a new garment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי אבהו's answer in Step 39 with an earlier source.
steps.raayaObject: The non-literal reading of 'spread the garment' according to the רבנן
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא explaining the פסוק as both sides' witnesses being examined

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: it means a real cloth
steps.stepSummary: In the same ברייתא, רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says the words mean exactly what they say: an actual cloth.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: The words are as they are written, a real garment.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with the other opinion. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads the פסוק simply, as a real sheet.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This fits his view from Step 31 that the claim only applies if the husband had relations with her. Since there were relations, there really is a sheet to spread out. So the ברייתא shows the same disagreement between the רבנן and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.

keyTerms.meaning: The words are as they are written (read literally)

steps.whatToRemember: The רבנן read every phrase of the פסוק as being about faithfulness and witnesses, so no relations are needed. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב reads them literally: relations, physical signs, and a real cloth.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
The words are as they are written,
an actual garment.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: דְּבָרִים כִּכְתָבָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other opinion in the same ברייתא as Step 40.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Spread the garment' refers to a real cloth, consistent with requiring relations for the claim.

steps.title: The defamer is the one place the Torah distinguishes typical from unusual relations
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that the תורה nowhere punishes typical and unusual relations differently, except in the case of מוציא שם רע. There the husband is liable only if he was with her, even in an unusual way, and then claims she was with someone else in the typical way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר רב יעקב בר גיורי sent a message in the name of רבי יוחנן: In the whole תורה, the verses never treat typical relations and unusual relations differently when it comes to lashes or punishments. But with the husband who spreads a bad name about his wife, the תורה does make a difference. He is only liable if he was with her, even in an unusual way, and then defames her about typical relations.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching from רבי יוחנן about the exact conditions under which the husband who falsely accuses his wife is punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everywhere else in the תורה, relations in a typical or an unusual way count the same for punishments like מלקות. מוציא שם רע is the one exception. The husband must have been with her, and an unusual way is enough. His false claim must be that she was with another man in the typical way, meaning she was no longer a virgin.

keyTerms.meaning: The husband who spreads a false bad name about his wife, claiming she was not a virgin
In an unusual, not natural way
Sent a message, usually from ארץ ישראל to בבל

steps.confusionAlert: There are two different acts here. The husband's own act can be in an unusual way. The thing he falsely accuses her of is typical relations with another man. Don't mix up which act each phrase is describing.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁלַח רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר רַב יַעֲקֹב בַּר גִּיּוֹרֵי
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Rav Yaakov bar Giyyorei sent a message
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
Although we have not found
in the entire Torah
that the verse made a distinction
between relations in the typical way
and relations in an unusual way
regarding lashes or punishments,
but with the defamer, it did make a distinction:

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב עַד שֶׁיִּבְעוֹל שֶׁלֹּא כְּדַרְכָּהּ,
phrases.english: he is not liable unless he was with her, even in an unusual way,
and he defames her about typical relations.
phrases.notes: His false claim is that another man was with her in the typical way, so she wasn't a virgin.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁלַח רַבִּי יִצְחָק בַּר רַב יַעֲקֹב בַּר גִּיּוֹרֵי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the argument between the רבנן and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב about how to read the פסוקים of מוציא שם רע, a new ruling is brought about when the defamer is liable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The defamer is liable only if he was with his wife, even in an unusual way, and falsely claims she had typical relations with another man. This is the only place the תורה treats typical and unusual relations differently.

steps.title: Whose opinion does רבי יוחנן's ruling follow?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which side רבי יוחנן follows. It cannot be the רבנן, because by their reading the husband is liable even if he never was with her. The גמרא starts to test רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view, and the sentence continues in the next lines.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whose opinion is this? If it follows the רבנן, the husband should be liable even if he was not with her at all. If it follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling by checking it against both sides of the earlier argument. It is setting up a problem for the second side too, which is finished in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן said in the ברייתא (step 31) that the husband is punished 'whether he had relations or did not.' That clashes with רבי יוחנן, who says he is liable only if he was with her. The גמרא now turns to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who does require relations, to see if the ruling fits him.

keyTerms.meaning: According to whom? Whose opinion does this follow?
Was with her as a husband

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא here is not rejecting רבי יוחנן. It is testing which side of the earlier argument he could fit.

phrases.english: In accordance with whom?
If like the Rabbis,
phrases.notes: These are the רבנן of the ברייתא in step 31, who said he is punished whether or not he had relations with her.

phrases.english: he should be liable even though he was not with her.
If like Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests רבי יוחנן's ruling in step 42 against the two opinions of the ברייתא in step 31.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's requirement that the husband must have been with his wife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The רבנן explicitly hold he is liable even without relations ('בין בעל ובין לא בעל'), which contradicts רבי יוחנן's requirement. The test of רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's view continues in the next lines.
